fix.description: In AuthService.refreshToken, load the session by id. Throw UnauthorizedException if it is missing or if session.hash !== data.hash. Then generate a new random hash with crypto.createHash('sha256').update(randomStringGenerator()).digest('hex'). Persist it with sessionService.update(session.id, { hash }) before calling getTokensData with that new hash. The old refresh token's hash then no longer matches and is rejected.

This strategy validates the refresh JWT payload and only checks that sessionId is present. It does not check the token's hash against the current session. If the service also skips that check, a replayed token passes.

The refresh token is signed with the session id and hash. If refreshToken passes in the old hash instead of a newly generated one, the new refresh token is the same as the old one in effect, so rotation has no effect.
